51323882.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged human LDHA in absence of NAD+ by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The ITC experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, UK) at 25 °C. The protein solution (100 μL, 10 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand solution (200 μL, 100 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.4) containing 150 mM NaCl. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The ligand was injected in 20 steps of 2 μL each, with a 120 s interval between injections. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) with a one-site binding model. The control experiment was performed by titrating the ligand into the buffer without protein.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Fig. 4. Biochemical activity of compound 9. (A) Binding affinities (Kd) of 9 bound to hLDH5 in the presence of or absence of NAD+. (B) EC50 value of 9 against hLDH5. (C) Lactate formation in NCI-H1975 cell after treatment of 9 for 4 h.
original_paragraph.Results section: To further prove 9 interacted with hLDH5, we titrated 9 into hLDH5 buffer solution by employing an isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiment, the Kd value was 1.02 μM in the presence of NAD+, while drop to 43.2 μM in the absence of NAD+, suggesting NAD+ was involved in the interaction between 9 and hLDH5, which is in consistence with the docking result in Fig. 3. Similarly, the Gen140 exhibited the same binding model, which interacted with NAD+, and formed hydrogen bond interactions with Asn137, Arg169 and His192 in hLDHA. Inhibiting of hLDH5 could lead to the reduction of lactate formation in cancer cell. To verify the hypothesis, NCI-H1975 cells were treated with 9 for 4 h, then culture medium in 6-well plates were collected, and the concentration of lactate in medium were measured. As shown in Fig. 4C, the lactate production was decreased with increment of 9, which is fully agreement with our hypothesis.
original_paragraph.Figure 4A thermogram data: With NAD+ Kd = 1.02 μM; w/o NAD+ Kd = 42.3 μM
